paragraphs: Powerfleet sells software and connected devices that pull fleet and warehouse operations into a single system it calls Unity. Buyers connect the vehicles running on the road along with the equipment moving goods inside a building.

The platform gathers readings from IoT devices, manufacturer systems and outside feeds, then turns them into compliance records for hours of service, inspections, temperature and driver qualifications. On the safety side, cameras watch road conditions while sensors inside the warehouse follow pedestrian proximity, equipment impacts and how operators behave. A separate set of tools collects the fuel and emissions figures a sustainability team has to report. The company points to an open API and packaged integrations rather than a rip-out of what a buyer already runs.

Powerfleet states that its headquarters sit in New Jersey. It describes a partner network and a physical footprint spanning more than a hundred countries. Technical staff are put at 450 people working around the globe.

quote.text: One pane of glass. One system of record.
